metadata.note: The Rochester, Syracuse and Eastern Railroad (RS&E, 1906-1917) and its successor the Rochester and Syracuse Railroad (1917-1931): an 87-mile double-track, catenary-electrified interurban connecting Rochester and Syracuse, NY via East Rochester, Fairport, Egypt, Macedon, Palmyra, Newark, Lyons, Clyde, Savannah, Port Byron, Weedsport, Jordan, Memphis, Warners, Amboy and Belle Isle. Part of the Beebe Syndicate, and the only one of its dozen interurban properties the Syndicate itself built from scratch. Paralleled the New York Central Railroad and the Erie Canal for most of its length. Abandoned June 28, 1931 amid the broader Depression-era collapse of interurban traction.

metadata.geometry_sources: See each feature's geometry_source/geometry_quality -- mostly real-traced abandoned right-of-way and rail-trail, with a documented parallel-active-rail-line substitute for 3 gaps and straight-line placeholders elsewhere, all itemized with mileage.
not_yet_sourced: The Newark-Lyons stretch (~10.6km / 6.6mi) has no surviving OSM trace of the RS&E's own alignment and the parallel CSX line runs too far away (3.7km+) to use as a substitute there, so it is drawn as an unconfirmed straight line -- the weakest-sourced single stretch of the route.

The exact 1906-1917 street-by-street routing between Culver Road (the easternmost specifically-named Rochester street) and the Perinton trail head is not documented; a modern-road shortest path (via NY-441) is used instead.

Whether the Rochester and Syracuse Railroad (1917-1931) ran over exactly the same alignment throughout as the original RS&E, or whether any segments were relocated/abandoned early, is not established -- this dataset assumes route continuity for the full 1906-1931 span.
avg_speed_kmh is a rough estimate from end-to-end travel times, not a documented running speed; headway_min (60) is an unsourced placeholder -- no timetable was found.

The connecting Auburn and Northern Electric Railroad branch (used by Syracuse-bound passengers to change at Auburn before the direct 1909 Port Byron-Syracuse segment opened) is a separate company and is not included in this file.

properties.line: Rochester, Syracuse and Eastern: Rochester – Syracuse
properties.speed_source: Estimated from documented Syracuse-Rochester travel times: local service 3h15m and limited service 2h30m over ~87 miles, giving roughly 27-35 km/h average -- no direct source states an average speed, so 30 km/h is used as a round midpoint estimate.

segments.note: Part of the Beebe Syndicate (Clifford D. Beebe), a group of a dozen interurban/electric lines from Buffalo to Oswego -- RS&E was the only one the Syndicate itself designed and built rather than acquiring. Consent to build granted Sept 1, 1902; construction began summer 1904. Built in phases: Newark-Macedon and Macedon-Egypt by Aug 1906, Lyons-Fairport by Sept 1 1906, Rochester-Clyde open by 1907, Montezuma Marsh crossing to Port Byron finished July 23 1908 (first full Rochester-Syracuse trip July 29 1908, a 4-hour journey), and the direct Port Byron-Syracuse segment (bypassing the earlier Auburn routing) completed Dec 18 1909, cutting the trip to 2.5-3.25 hours. A double-track, catenary-electrified, standard-gauge line, 87 miles at full extent, with only one grade crossing with another railroad in its whole length; in 1912 carried over 4.3 million passengers. Reorganized 1913-1915 into the holding company Empire United Railways alongside other Beebe Syndicate properties; that reorganization failed and the line was back operating as RS&E by 1916, so it is not modeled as a separate colored segment here. A separate connecting company, the Auburn and Northern Electric Railroad, allowed passengers to change at Auburn for Syracuse before the direct 1909 line opened -- that Auburn branch is a different company and is not included in this feature.

properties.geometry_source: Routed primarily along the actual abandoned right-of-way of the Rochester, Syracuse and Eastern Railroad, traced from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass (overpass.openstreetmap.fr): 29 separate surviving fragments tagged railway=abandoned/disused/razed or highway=cycleway/path with name='Rochester, Syracuse and Eastern Railroad' / 'Rochester, Syracuse & Eastern' / 'Rochester, Syracuse & Eastern Trolley Trail' (the latter a real rail-trail in Perinton/Fairport), chained end-to-end in geographic order. Where the ROW is not preserved in OSM, three of the larger gaps (Macedon-Palmyra ~8.5km, Lyons-Clyde ~7.1km, Clyde-Savannah ~6.0km) are filled by routing along the CSX Rochester Subdivision (the historic New York Central line the RS&E is documented to have paralleled for most of its length), which runs within ~1.5km of the RS&E's own remnants at both ends of each of those gaps. All smaller gaps (most under 1.5km, one of 2.1km) are drawn as straight lines between the confirmed remnant endpoints. ONE large gap, Newark to Lyons (~10.6km), is also a straight line rather than a CSX substitute: the CSX line runs at least 3.7km from the RS&E's Newark-area remnant endpoint there, too far to treat as a reliable proxy, so this is the least-confirmed stretch of the whole route. The Rochester end (downtown to the Perinton trail head) and Syracuse end (Camillus to downtown) are present-day street routing: East Main Street/University Avenue (both specifically named in sources) then a modern-road path via NY-441 and local streets out to East Rochester on the Rochester end (the exact 1906-1917 street-by-street routing east of Culver Road is not sourced); Erie Boulevard West (built on the old Erie Canal alignment the RS&E is documented to have followed) then downtown streets on the Syracuse end. 1352 points, 142.87 km (88.78 mi) -- close to the 87-mile length reported in sources, a good sanity check on the overall route.
properties.geometry_quality: MOSTLY REAL-TRACED (real abandoned railbed/rail-trail geometry for roughly 70 of the route's ~87 miles), with the remainder split between a parallel-active-rail-line substitute (honest proxy, not the interurban's own alignment) for 3 gaps and straight-line placeholders for the rest, including one unconfirmed 10.6km stretch (Newark-Lyons) and modern street routing at both city ends. See geometry_source for the full breakdown. No leg is drawn as a later-era alignment than its own era -- the CSX Rochester Subdivision has carried freight/passenger rail on essentially this same alignment since the 19th century, predating the RS&E itself.

segments.note: Reorganized as the Rochester and Syracuse Railroad Co. after an Aug 28, 1917 foreclosure sale. Arthur W. Loasby, president; T.C. Cherry, VP/general manager; Elbert A. Hervey, treasurer. Offered parlor cars on limited trains (converted to freight service during WWI) and ran vacation excursions to regional parks/resorts; modernized with limited-service coaches and began using the Rochester Subway for city access around 1927-1928. Entered receivership in 1930, and the line was abandoned just after midnight on June 28, 1931, with the property dismantled and sold for scrap that year.
